residue.text: Protected observation: B9 carries the same ten-bracket packing mark as the others but physically contains nine. Retain incompatible accounts explicitly: mark-as-count predicts ten before correction and eleven after adding the spare; physical-shortfall predicts nine before correction and ten afterward. The former is already rejected by stipulated O6, not a live supported explanation. A packing mark cannot establish a correct completed release.

Feasible probe: record B9 first count within its mandatory inspection, then add the supplied spare, recount and seal without interruption. Nine on first count defeats mark-as-count; ten would contradict the protected stipulation. This distinguishes present-count accounts, not discrepancy causes. Replay proposed and hand-only schedules with the clock and ledger, recording unload identities, corrected counts, completed releases, both clerks occupied intervals, rack occupancy and remaining charge.

Defeat the proposed sequence if legal replay yields fewer than twelve correct releases by 13, insufficient whole-load unloading space, or transfer occupation above seven minutes. B9 discrepancy cause remains unknown; the probe cannot distinguish marking error from an earlier inventory change. Later request adaptation is unobserved. No empirical comparison or global optimality proof is supplied. No additional resources, arrivals or window losses are admissible.

summary.text: Preserve B9 marked ten but containing nine. Count, add the available spare, recount ten and seal over two inspection minutes. Mark-as-count is an explicitly rejected account. All twelve demanded carriers still require correct sealed completion by minute 13.

Proposed finite-model calculation: trolley B4-B7 during 0-3, trolley B8-B11 during 3-6, hand carry B12 during 6-7. Inspect continuously: B1-B8 finish at 1-8, B9 occupies 8-10, B10-B12 finish 11-13. Completion-first unloading predicts no waiting, nine source unloads, twelve correct releases, seven transfer-clerk minutes and thirteen inspection-clerk minutes. Closest rival uses consecutive hand trips for B4-B12 during 0-9 with identical inspections: predicted completion at 13 and nine transfer minutes.

Ledger replay tests releases, burden and capacity; B9 first count separates rejected ten-count prediction from protected nine-count prediction before correction. These are calculated predictions, not observed runs. Any missed deadline, blocked unloading invalidating the sequence, or occupation above seven defeats it. Discrepancy cause and later demand adaptation remain unknown; global best operation is unproved.
